bull_case.title: Bull case: the hike is already priced and credit stays calm

contradicting_signals.claim: Credit markets still show no stress: HY OAS is 2.70 at the 10.93rd percentile and IG OAS 0.80, leaving the liquidity and credit dimension at 33.31 on a flat trend -- the missing link in the risk case.
Realized volatility is far below implied: 8.742 (risk score 10.0) against a VIX of 17.84, and the volatility dimension scores only 31.93, so this is a repricing rather than a stress event.
Risk appetite outside rates is intact: bitcoin rose +1.48155 to 77919.0, ether +1.33745 and solana +2.00797, so the bitcoin-down cross-asset signal did not trigger, and gold fell -0.7764.

Breakevens fell against an energy shock: the 5-year breakeven is 2.32 and the 10-year 2.36, both lower even as Brent crude traded higher after the Saudi pipeline shutdown, which reads as a growth-negative impulse rather than an inflation-expectation one.

summary: Pre-market brief. The composite risk score stands at 45.68, up 0.47 on the day, with the risk level still caution and the regime still goldilocks; fact-layer confidence is 0.9301. In the last US session equities advanced broadly -- 19 of 22 sectors/themes rose, led by networking +3.5075, AI infrastructure +3.3612 and data centers +2.7182 -- while memory was the single sharp exception at -5.1964. Implied volatility finally moved: the VIX rose to 17.84 from 16.46, entering the 51.11th percentile, ending the stretch in which vol refused to confirm the rates move. Credit did not follow: HY OAS held at 2.70 and IG OAS at 0.80. The binding constraint remains the long end, which broke higher again -- the 10-year Treasury yield rose to 4.95 from 4.83 (99.92nd percentile) and the 2-year to 4.56 from 4.43, lifting the 10-year real rate to 2.55 at the 100th percentile, a fresh extreme. With CPI at 3.35302 and an implied policy rate of 4.08 against an effective fed funds rate of 3.63, a hike is priced as the base case. Asia handed the pre-market a weaker hand: all 11 tracked A-share AI names closed lower, the worst at -3.9485. Brent crude pushed higher after the Saudi pipeline shutdown, keeping the energy impulse live, yet breakevens fell -- a growth-negative read. Pre-market bias: defensive, with the missing confirmation still a credit-spread break rather than a volatility spike.

supporting_signals.claim: The equity tape advanced broadly in the last US session: 19 of 22 sectors/themes rose, led by networking +3.5075, AI infrastructure +3.3612 and data centers +2.7182, and the trend dimension rose to 44.81 with price 7.0084 above the 200-day average.
The front end joined the move rather than anchoring it: the 2-year yield rose to 4.56 from 4.43, leaving the 10Y/2Y curve at 0.39, so the selloff is not purely a term-premium story.
The overnight Asia session diverged from the US hardware rebound: all 11 tracked A-share AI names closed lower, with the worst at -3.9485 and 603986.sh at -3.8888.
Participation stopped improving: the share of names above their 200-day average is 0.5806 and new highs only matched new lows at 0.0194, so the index-level advance is not corroborated by breadth.

top_risk_drivers.claim: The long end broke higher again and the real rate set a fresh extreme: the 10-year Treasury yield rose to 4.95 from 4.83 (99.92nd percentile, risk score 99.84) and the 10-year real rate to 2.55 from 2.46, putting it at the 100th percentile, with the macro dimension's 62.73 the heaviest of the six.

A hike is priced as the base case: CPI at 3.35302 with core at 2.44616 has pushed the implied policy rate to 4.08, a hike, against an effective fed funds rate of 3.63 -- the first tightening priced under the new Fed leadership.

Implied volatility finally moved: the VIX rose to 17.84 from 16.46 (+1.38) into the 51.11th percentile, ending the stretch in which vol refused to confirm the rates move, while realized volatility remains far lower at 8.742.

Leadership stayed narrow and internally split: semis relative strength is -13.7948 and small-cap relative strength -4.1194, the new-highs ratio is only 0.0194, and the memory theme fell -5.1964 while networking rose +3.5075.

Cross-asset confirmation is pinned at 0.5 -- 4 of the 8 production-scoring signals are triggered -- with the dollar at 118.0732 (15.35th percentile) and copper at -0.4328, leaving the cross-asset dimension at exactly neutral, 50.0.

watch_next: Advance Retail Sales on 2026-09-16 is the nearest high-importance release, with the FOMC meeting on 2026-09-28 the next policy test.
Whether credit finally confirms: HY OAS moving above 2.70, or IG OAS above 0.80, is the single most important missing confirmation.
Whether the VIX extends beyond the 51.11th percentile and realized volatility closes the gap to 8.742, which would turn a repricing into a stress signal.
Whether the memory theme's -5.1964 decline spreads to the wider semiconductor complex, and whether the Korean memory makers' electricity dispute affects supply.

The AI-slowdown narrative: safety-pause headlines and the optical-module supply chain are the two threads most likely to move the AI complex, alongside whether the 11 A-share AI names stabilise after Monday's close.
what_changed_today: The 10-year Treasury yield rose to 4.95 from 4.83 and the 2-year to 4.56 from 4.43, lifting the real rate to 2.55 at the 100th percentile, a fresh extreme.
The VIX rose to 17.84 from 16.46, ending the stretch in which implied volatility refused to confirm the rates move.
The total risk score rose 0.47 to 45.68, still caution, with the regime unchanged at goldilocks and confidence at 0.9301.
The AI complex split internally: networking rose +3.5075 and AI infrastructure +3.3612, while the memory theme fell -5.1964 and Micron was -0.22.
Credit did not follow the rates move: HY OAS went to 2.70 from 2.71 and IG OAS to 0.80 from 0.81, while reverse repo rose to 5.255 from 4.736.
